statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold because the completed August month-end session traversed its range in both directions with repeatedly successful retracements, while Stress stays elevated on Brent near 90 dollars, a 4.73 percent 10-year yield and roughly 60 percent implied odds of a September rate hike.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning. The Nasdaq-100 absorbed a 3 percent crude advance and a fresh Middle East escalation and still closed 0.08 percent higher at 29,456.97, retracements were repeatedly successful rather than failed, and VIX finished near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range even as it rose 3.4 percent on the day. The cross-asset picture is conflicting rather than aligned: oil and long-end yields rose together while megacap performance split sharply, with Tesla up 5.5 percent and Nvidia up 1.5 percent against Amazon down 2.5 percent and Alphabet down 2.1 percent, and semiconductors were positive across all seven tracked names. That dispersion describes rotation, not the persistent one-way index structure that defines Tail. Identifiable conditional risk is concentrated in the 13:45 to 15:00 UTC window on 1 September, when the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI, the U.S. cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases arrive against a hawkish rate backdrop. CME equity futures are inside the 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt, so no live price path can form this hour, and any Asian-session gap remains an unobserved conditional risk rather than observed structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 ends August at 29,456.97 with Globex halted, while Brent above 90 dollars, a 4.73 percent 10-year and hawkish September repricing keep Stress elevated
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August month-end session at 29,456.97, up 23.54 points or 0.08 percent, after opening at 29,404.29 and traversing a 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions. The close sits 27 points, about 0.09 percent, below the session high. That price path is the central observation for Tail: retracements were deep and repeatedly successful, pullbacks were not unusually shallow, and no chain of failed retracements followed by repeated extension formed at any point in the session. CME equity index futures entered their daily 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt with the September E-mini contract last at 29,491.75, up 0.10 percent across a 29,274.75 to 29,545.50 Globex range, so no live price path can form during the current clock hour.

The macro backdrop is materially more stressed than the index path. U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island that were being prepared to deploy sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly a fifth of world oil shipments. Brent rose 3.0 percent to 90.74 dollars and WTI 3.49 percent to 86.31 dollars. The crude move fed directly into the inflation channel: the Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 10-year Treasury constant maturity at 4.73 percent and the 30-year at 5.22 percent for 31 August, with the 10-year touching 4.76 percent intraday, its highest since January 2025, and the 2-year at 4.34 percent. Following Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address on 28 August, in which he warned that underlying inflation trends had not meaningfully improved, fed funds futures moved to roughly 60 percent implied odds of a quarter-point September rate hike, up from about one in three before the speech.

Cross-asset evidence is conflicting rather than aligned, which under the operative risk definition raises Stress and lowers directional conviction without raising Tail. The Dow fell 0.7 percent and the S&P 500 0.3 percent while the Nasdaq-100 finished higher, so index-level dispersion was wide. Megacap performance split, with Tesla up 5.5 percent and Nvidia up 1.5 percent after agreeing to invest 3.5 billion dollars in MediaTek, against Amazon down 2.5 percent on reports the Federal Trade Commission and 22 states are suing over advertising pricing disclosures, Alphabet down 2.1 percent and Microsoft down 1.2 percent. All seven tracked semiconductors closed higher, averaging 1.5 percent. Sector breadth was split, with technology up 0.22 percent against communication services down 1.5 percent. VIX rose 3.4 percent to 14.92 but settled near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range, and VIX futures eased on the shared cross-asset feed, both of which argue against an alignment of volatility with the energy and rates impulse.

The forward path is therefore scored as conditional risk rather than observed structure. The overnight sequence runs through the Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC, the Tokyo cash open at 00:00 UTC, which produced the prior session's published Tail peak of 15 as Asia repriced the Larak Island strike, and the European cash open at 07:00 UTC. The concentrated catalyst hour is 14:00 UTC on 1 September, when ISM Manufacturing PMI with consensus near 55 and JOLTS Job Openings with consensus of 7.3 to 7.4 million release simultaneously, half an hour after the U.S. cash open and with the ISM prices-paid component consensus near 70. That is the only hour of the 24-hour forecast mapped above the low Tail band. The published danger window is deliberately narrow at 13:45 to 15:00 UTC, spanning the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI, the double release and the window in which a delayed second leg routed through the Treasury market would appear. The unresolved Strait of Hormuz situation remains the one credible discontinuity mechanism that could invalidate this assessment through a gap rather than through an observable intraday path.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours run from the late Sunday Globex session through the August month-end U.S. cash close. Published Tail began at 5 in an orderly regime, rose to 15 by the 00:00 UTC Asian repricing of the Larak Island strike, eased back to 5 through the European morning, spiked to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse, and then settled between 9 and 13 across the entire U.S. session. Stress climbed from 32 to a peak of 55 as oil, long-end yields and September rate-hike odds repriced hawkishly, and finished at 53. Every one of the 24 hours mapped to EA_ON and green, and no hour is unavailable. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout, reflecting continuously verified levels rather than inferred structure.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the current Globex maintenance halt through the Asian and European sessions and into the first September U.S. afternoon. Conditional Tail starts at 10 during the halt, when no price path can form, drifts between 10 and 13 overnight with the 00:00 UTC Tokyo open as the highest overnight reading, firms to 13 in the 09:00 UTC hour that carried the prior session's Tail peak, and rises to a conditional peak of 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That is the only hour mapped to WATCH and yellow; the other 23 hours remain EA_ON and green. Conditional Stress peaks at 64 in the same hour and otherwise holds in the 49 to 60 band, sustained by Brent near 90 dollars and a 30-year yield above 5.2 percent. Forecast confidence decays from 87 to 69 across the horizon because evidence quality for distant hours is necessarily weaker. The danger window stays narrow at 13:45 to 15:00 UTC. None of the forecast structure is observed; a Strait of Hormuz discontinuity arriving as an overnight gap is the principal way this path would be invalidated.
